name: Fae Herald
author: Frederik Rosendahl-Kaa

sections.description:
Fae Herald helps you maintain a secure WordPress site by monitoring when your installed plugins were last updated and alerting you to potential security risks.

Features

Last Version Release Monitoring
* Shows “Latest Version Released” date for recently maintained plugins (under 6 months)
* Shows time in months for plugins updated 6-12 months ago
* Warning alert when a plugin hasn’t been updated in over 1 year
* Critical alert when a plugin hasn’t been updated in over 2 years

Closed Plugin Detection
* Automatically detects if a plugin has been closed or removed from wordpress.org
* Displays the reason why the plugin was closed
* Shows the date when the plugin was removed
* Full explanation from WordPress.org about the closure

Smart Integration
* Information displayed directly in your plugin list after plugin metadata
* Weekly automatic background checks via WordPress cron (staggered with 20-second intervals)
* Only checks plugins from wordpress.org (skips premium plugins with custom Update URIs)
* Automatic cleanup when plugins are deleted
* Tracks plugin installation and activation/deactivation timestamps
* Screen Options – Toggle visibility of different status types per user preference

Why Use This Plugin?

Many WordPress sites use plugins that are no longer maintained or have been removed from wordpress.org. This poses serious security risks:

  • Unmaintained plugins often have known vulnerabilities
  • They no longer receive security updates
  • Closed plugins may have been removed due to security issues
  • Outdated plugins can cause compatibility issues

Fae Herald gives you a comprehensive overview so you can act proactively to protect your site.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Fae Herald checks begin automatically in the background (staggered every 20 seconds per plugin)
  3. Initial data collection completes within a few minutes depending on number of plugins
  4. View Fae Herald directly on your Plugins page (wp-admin/plugins.php)
  5. Checks run automatically once per week to keep information current
  6. Newly installed plugins are automatically checked within 20 seconds
  7. Plugin installation and activation/deactivation timestamps are tracked
  8. Customize which status types to display using Screen Options (top right corner)
  9. Take action on outdated or closed plugins

Privacy Policy

This plugin does not collect, store, or transmit any personal data. It only:
* Queries the public WordPress.org Plugin API for plugin information
* Stores Fae Herald data locally in your WordPress database
* Does not track users or send data to external services
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/fae-herald/, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. You’ll see a notice indicating checks are starting in the background
  4. Fae Herald information will appear as it becomes available (approximately 20 seconds per plugin)
  5. View status information on the Plugins page
sections.faq:
Does this plugin slow down my site?

No. Status checks run in the background via WordPress cron, staggered with 20-second intervals between each plugin to prevent server load. The plugin list page shows data stored in the database with minimal performance impact. Checks happen once weekly automatically.

What happens if a plugin is closed?

You’ll see a red warning with the reason and closure date, allowing you to find an alternative or remove the plugin.

Can I manually trigger a status update?

Yes! Each plugin row on the Plugins page includes a “Refresh Status” link. Clicking this will perform an immediate status check for that specific plugin (bypasses the cron system). This works even if you have disabled automatic background checks.

Does it work with plugins not on wordpress.org?

No. The plugin only monitors plugins available on wordpress.org. Plugins not hosted on wordpress.org or plugins with custom update URIs are automatically skipped and will show a message indicating they are being ignored.

Can I ignore specific plugins from being checked?

Yes! Some plugins may appear in the WordPress.org repository but are actually managed elsewhere (e.g., WPML). To prevent false warnings for these plugins, you can add them to the ignored plugins list.

Important: Do not edit the file in the plugin directory directly, as your changes will be lost when the plugin is updated.

Instead, follow these steps:

  1. Create a folder named fae-herald in your active theme directory
  2. Copy the file wp-content/plugins/fae-herald/assets/ignored-plugins.json to wp-content/themes/your-theme/fae-herald/ignored-plugins.json

  3. Edit the copied file and add the plugin slug with a reason:

    {
    “plugin-slug”: {
    “reason”: “Explanation why this plugin is ignored”
    }
    }

The plugin will automatically use your theme’s version of the file if it exists. Ignored plugins will display a gray notice showing they are on the ignored list along with the reason you specified.

What do the different warnings mean?

  • Blue Normal: Latest version released within the past 6 months shows exact date, after 6 months to 12 months shows “X months ago”
  • Orange Warning: Plugin not updated in over 1 year
  • Red Critical: Plugin not updated in over 2 years or has been closed
  • Gray Notice: Not so important information (e.g., non-wordpress.org plugins)

Is the plugin translation ready?

Yes! The plugin is fully translation-ready with:
* Complete .pot template file for translators
* Danish translation included (da_DK)
* Modern .l10n.php format for improved performance (WordPress 6.5+)
* Traditional .mo files for backward compatibility
* Text domain: fae-herald

How long does the initial scan take?

The initial scan depends on the number of plugins you have installed. With a 20-second interval between checks, a site with 20 plugins will complete in approximately 6-7 minutes. You can leave the page and continue working while checks run in the background.

Does the plugin track when I install or activate/deactivate plugins?

Yes, the plugin automatically records timestamps when:
* A plugin is installed (shows installation date for newly installed plugins that haven’t been activated yet)
* A plugin is activated
* A plugin is deactivated (shows deactivation date and time)

This information helps you track plugin lifecycle events on your site.

Can I hide certain types of status information?

Yes! Click on “Screen Options” in the top right corner of the Plugins page to toggle visibility of:
* Critical Issues (closed plugins, 2+ years old)
* Warnings (1+ year without updates)
* Last Update Information
* Plugin State (installed/deactivated)
* Non-WordPress.org Plugins

These settings are saved per user, so each administrator can customize their own view.

How to change cron intervals and spacing delay?

You can customize the frequency of background checks and spacing delay by adding the following constants to your wp-config.php file:
define( ‘FAE_HERALD_CRON_INTERVAL’, 604800 ); // in seconds (default: 604800 = 1 week)
define( ‘FAE_HERALD_CRON_SPACING_DELAY’, 60 ); // in seconds (default: 60 seconds)

How to disable automatic background checks?

If you want to disable automatic background checks but still use manual “Refresh Status” for individual plugins, add this constant to your wp-config.php file:

define( 'FAE_HERALD_DISABLE_AUTOMATIC_CRON', true );

With this enabled, you can still manually refresh status for any plugin using the “Refresh Status” link on the Plugins page.

Delete data on deactivation

By default, plugin data is only deleted when the plugin is uninstalled. If you want to delete all plugin data when deactivating the plugin, you can enable this behavior by adding the following constant to your wp-config.php file:

define( 'FAE_HERALD_DELETE_DATA_ON_DEACTIVATE', true );

When this is set to true, all plugin data will be automatically deleted when you deactivate the plugin. This is useful for testing or if you want to start fresh.
